cathedral.title: The Cathedral of St. James
cathedral.text: St. James Cathedral is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Šibenik, Croatia. Built in the 15th and 16th centuries, it is a masterpiece of Gothic and Renaissance architecture. The exterior is adorned with sculptures and unique faces, while the interior features stunning stone work and stained glass windows. The cathedral's magnificent dome dominates the city's skyline, and visitors can see an ornate altar and baptismal font inside. The exterior of the cathedral is adorned with numerous sculptures, including 71 unique sculpted faces that are said to represent the citizens of Šibenik at the time of the cathedral's construction.

krka.title: NP Krka
krka.text: Krka National Park is a breathtakingly beautiful natural reserve in Croatia, famous for its magnificent waterfalls, crystal clear pools, and stunning natural scenery. The park spans over 142 square kilometers, with a diverse array of flora and fauna, including over 200 bird species. The park's main attraction is the Skradinski Buk waterfall, which cascades down a series of limestone steps and creates a mesmerizing visual display. Visitors can swim in the crystal-clear pools at the base of the waterfall, or take a boat tour to explore the park's various waterways and enjoy the surrounding nature.

kornati.title: NP Kornati
kornati.text: Kornati National Park, a breathtaking natural wonder nestled in the heart of Croatia! Known as a sailor's paradise, this archipelago consists of 109 stunning islands, islets, and reefs, forming an awe-inspiring maze of rugged beauty in the Adriatic Sea. The islands are characterized by their stark limestone cliffs, rising majestically from the crystal-clear turquoise waters. These dramatic formations have been shaped by the elements over thousands of years, creating a landscape that is truly one-of-a-kind.

stNicholas.title: St Nicholas' Fortress
stNicholas.text: St Nicholas' Fortress at the entrance to the St Anthony's Channel in Šibenik represents a unique Renaissance building of Venetian fortification architecture and an exceptional monument of the world's architectural heritage. It was constructed on the islet of Ljuljevac, where once was the Benedictine monastery of St Nicholas, after which the fortress was named. The construction of the fortress, based on Gian Girolamo San Micheli's design, commenced in 1540 after the fall of Skradin under the Ottoman rule, when the Venetians were forced to strengthen the defence of Šibenik port, which was the most important port on the east coast of the Adriatic Sea.

stAnthony.title: St Anthony's Channel
stAnthony.text: The St Anthony's Channel is part of a wider location called Channel – Port, which represents a significant landscape protected in 1974. It is more than 2000 metres long and 140 – 220 metres wide. It is a gateway to the open sea and entrance to Šibenik. At the same time, the channel represents a symbolical end of the Krka River, since it is where the river flows into the Adriatic Sea. It can be seen from all parts of Šibenik and despite being in close proximity to the city and easily accessible, it used to be isolated and unknown due to historical circumstances. Apart from the obvious natural attractions and a magnificent panoramic view of Šibenik, the Šibenik archipelago and St Nicholas' Fortress, the channel treasures numerous cultural and natural values.

villaDetails.introText: Your Perfect Croatian Retreat in Šibenik
villaDetails.description:
Villa Mandalina is a beautiful, modern holiday home built in 2019, located in the peaceful neighborhood of Mandalina, just 2 km from the historic city center of Šibenik. This stunning property offers 170m² of living space on 180m² of land with a private heated pool and sea views, perfect for families or groups looking for a relaxing Croatian getaway.

The villa features 4 spacious bedrooms and 4 bathrooms, comfortably accommodating up to 10 guests. Three bedrooms have king-size beds with private en-suite bathrooms, while the fourth has two single beds. Each room is equipped with air conditioning and satellite TV for your comfort.

guide.title: Šibenik and the Dalmatian coast
guide.intro: Šibenik is one of the oldest towns on the Croatian coast and sits right in the middle of Dalmatia. From Villa Mandalina you can walk the old town's stone lanes in the morning, swim under waterfalls in the afternoon and be back at the pool for sunset.

beaches.title: Beaches
beaches.text: The nearest beach is 4 km from the villa, and there are pebble beaches and swimming spots all along the coast around Šibenik. Many families like to split the day: a morning at the sea, an afternoon at the villa's heated pool.

base.title: Why stay in Šibenik?
base.text: Šibenik is quieter than Split or Dubrovnik but just as rich in history, and it puts two national parks within easy reach. It's an easy base for a Croatian holiday by car, with the old town, shops and restaurants close by.

cta.title: Stay at Villa Mandalina
cta.text: A heated private pool, four bedrooms and sea views, 2 km from Šibenik's old town.

items.q: Is Šibenik good for a family holiday?
items.a: Yes. Šibenik is calmer than the bigger Dalmatian cities, with beaches, national parks and a compact old town that is easy to explore with children.

items.q: How far is Krka National Park from Šibenik?
items.a: Krka National Park is a short drive inland from Šibenik, which makes it an easy half-day or day trip from Villa Mandalina.

items.q: Can you visit the Kornati islands from Šibenik?
items.a: Yes. Boat excursions to the Kornati National Park run from Šibenik and the nearby coast during the season.

items.q: What UNESCO sites are in Šibenik?
items.a: The Cathedral of St James and St Nicholas Fortress are both on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
